place.source_title: John Eckert House, 510 West Second Street

brief: One-storey brick shotgun house, one room wide and several deep, with a street facade of pressed sheet metal in an Italianate style: pilasters, tall round-headed windows and a heavy bracketed cornice hiding the gable behind. A low iron fence runs along the sidewalk; built for a tinsmith, it sits among two-storey brick neighbours. Record has 1 photo plus 3 measured drawing sheets.

facade.notes: the John Eckert House (1872): a one-storey Italianate front on a narrow deep lot -- an elaborate pressed-metal or cast front with a bracketed and panelled cornice, rusticated corner quoins, three tall openings under arched hoods with keystone cartouches; a long plain brick side wall running back; a low iron fence at the walk

why.note: a narrow, deep lot: one room wide, rooms in a line back from a show front
catalogue cast-iron and pressed-metal ornament put city style on a small house
